news.title: Argentina hit with sanctions for Falklands banner, World Cup final brawl
news.lede: Argentina have been hit with major sanctions by Fifa over their display of a Falkland Islands banner, while two players face lengthy bans for their actions in the World Cup final. After beating England 2-1 in their Fifa World Cup semi-final, Argentina players paraded a banner that read “Las Malvinas son Argentinas”, which translates to the Falklands belong to Argentina. Three EPL players, including Manchester United’s Lisandro Martinez and former Tottenham Hotspurs players Cristian Romero and Giovani Lo Celso, were pictured with the banner. The rivalry between the two nations over the islands was a hot topic before the match, with the tension being traced back to the South American nation’s invasion of the Falklands in 1982.

news.title: BREAKING: FIFA drops biggest punishment in World Cup history
news.lede: Four Argentina players have been suspended after FIFA handed down heavy sanctions for the ugly fight that followed their World Cup final loss to Spain. Football’s governing body announced in the days following the final, which Spain won 1-0 for their second title, that they were undertaking a disciplinary investigation after several La Albiceleste players reacted to defeat by sparking a stoush with their Spanish counterparts after the final whistle. news.title: Britain wants to host the World Cup in 2042
news.lede: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham has floated the idea of ​​hosting the 2042 FIFA World Cup in the United Kingdom, APA reports citing The Times newspaper. According to the report, Burnham put forward his idea at a meeting with city mayors held in the prime minister's new office in Manchester. The prime minister is reportedly in talks with the Football Association and the English Premier League about the possibility of submitting a bid to host the tournament. According to The Times, Burnham's government is also preparing to bid to host the 2040 Olympic and Paralympic Games.

news.title: FIFA hands out suspensions, hefty fines after Argentina-Spain World Cup final brawl
news.lede: FIFA has handed down significant suspensions to Argentine players Leandro Paredes and Nahuel Molina, alongside a hefty fine to the Argentine Football Association (AFA), following a post-match brawl in the World Cup final against Spain and other disciplinary breaches. Argentina's Leandro Paredes received a 10-match suspension for his part in a brawl after his team lost to Spain in the World Cup final while teammate Nahuel Molina was suspended for seven games, FIFA announced on Friday. A brief scuffle erupted at the final whistle when Argentina midfielder Paredes shoved Spain's Gavi to the ground as the European champions' substitutes rushed onto the pitch to celebrate. Paredes faced three assault counts while Molina faced two.

news.title: Gianni Infantino 'plotted U15s World Cup hosted next to DISNEYLAND with 211 teams representing every Fifa nation'
news.lede: GIANNI INFANTINO reportedly tried to launch an Under-15s World Cup next to Disneyland featuring all 211 Fifa nations. The under-fire Fifa chief is said to have plotted a youth “festival of football” inspired by Little League in baseball. Infantino – who is already facing calls to resign after trying to sell off chunks of the World Cup – was hoping to commercialise the U15 tournament. The event would have taken place at the ESPN Wide World Of Sports Complex close to Disneyworld in Orlando, Florida, according to the Athletic.

news.title: Tom Bischof talks about his summer break, watching the World Cup from home
news.lede: Tom Bischof has a remarkable mindset at such a young age: he played less than he would’ve liked for Bayern Munich last season and was unceremoniously left out of Germany’s squad for the World Cup.
